prompt:
In the push-relabel maximum flow algorithm with the highest-label selection rule, consider the effect of the gap heuristic. Which of the following correctly explains why the gap heuristic improves performance?

A) It eliminates the need for BFS to rebuild the level graph by detecting when a height value has no vertices assigned to it, causing all vertices above that height to be marked as unreachable from the sink.
B) It reduces the number of saturating pushes by preferentially selecting edges with higher residual capacity.
C) It replaces the global relabeling step with localized height updates that propagate along reverse edges.
D) It prevents the algorithm from pushing flow out of vertices whose height exceeds the maximum possible shortest-path distance from source to sink.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the Hopcroft-Karp algorithm for maximum bipartite matching. Which condition guarantees that the BFS phase of the algorithm has found a maximal set of vertex-disjoint shortest augmenting paths?

A) The BFS proceeds until all vertices at distance d from the source are exhausted, where d is the distance to the farthest reachable unmatched vertex.
B) The BFS builds a layered graph from all free left vertices, and each DFS augmentation saturates one edge at the current shortest distance, after which that edge is removed from the layered graph.
C) The algorithm terminates when the number of augmenting paths found in a single DFS phase is less than the size of the matching.
D) The BFS phase constructs the layered graph from all free left vertices and terminates when all free right vertices are at the same minimum distance.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the context of Delaunay triangulation of a set of points in the plane in general position (no three collinear, no four cocircular), which of the following statements is true about the relationship between the Delaunay triangulation and the Euclidean minimum spanning tree (EMST)?

A) The EMST is always a superset of the Delaunay triangulation, containing all Delaunay edges plus additional edges necessary for connectivity.
B) The Delaunay triangulation is always a subgraph of the EMST, and all EMST edges are Delaunay edges.
C) The EMST is a subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation, meaning every edge of the EMST appears in the Delaunay triangulation.
D) There is no guaranteed containment relationship; the EMST and Delaunay triangulation are independent structures.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the A* search algorithm for graph traversal, suppose the heuristic h(n) is admissible but NOT consistent (monotonic). Which of the following best describes the consequences for optimality and the required modifications?

A) A* with an admissible but inconsistent heuristic is guaranteed to find the optimal path without any modifications, because admissibility alone suffices for optimality.
B) A* may fail to find the optimal path with an inconsistent heuristic and must be modified to use a bidirectional search instead.
C) A* with an admissible but inconsistent heuristic remains optimal only if the algorithm re-opens closed nodes when a better g-value is discovered, which may increase the running time.
D) An inconsistent heuristic cannot be admissible, so this situation cannot arise.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the Li Chao segment tree for dynamic convex hull trick queries. In which scenario does the Li Chao tree maintain its O(log C) per-operation guarantee (where C is the coordinate range) while a deque-based CHT implementation fails?

A) When slopes are inserted in arbitrary order and query x-coordinates are also arbitrary.
B) When slopes are inserted in monotonic order but queries are in arbitrary order.
C) When both slopes and queries are monotonic in the same direction.
D) When slopes are inserted in arbitrary order but queries are monotonic.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

For the divide-and-conquer DP optimization to apply to the recurrence dp[i][j] = min_{k < j} (dp[i-1][k] + cost(k+1, j)), which of the following conditions must hold?

A) The cost function satisfies the quadrangle inequality: cost(a, c) + cost(b, d) <= cost(a, d) + cost(b, c) for all a <= b <= c <= d.
B) The optimal decision point opt[i][j] = argmin_k (dp[i-1][k] + cost(k+1, j)) is monotonic in j for each fixed i.
C) The cost function is convex in its second argument.
D) Both conditions A and B must hold simultaneously.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the 2-SAT algorithm using implication graphs and strongly connected components, which of the following conditions is both necessary and sufficient for the Boolean formula to be unsatisfiable?

A) The implication graph contains any directed cycle.
B) There exists a variable x such that the nodes representing x and not x belong to the same strongly connected component.
C) The number of clauses exceeds the number of variables by a factor greater than 2.
D) The implication graph, when viewed as an undirected graph, is not bipartite.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the Tonelli-Shanks algorithm for computing modular square roots modulo an odd prime p. Let p - 1 = Q * 2^S where Q is odd. In the worst case, what is the expected number of iterations of the main loop that reduces the exponent S?

A) O(log log p) iterations on average, but O(S) = O(log p) in the worst case.
B) Exactly S iterations, each requiring O(log p) modular multiplications.
C) O(1) expected iterations regardless of S, because a quadratic non-residue is always found quickly.
D) O(sqrt(p)) iterations because the algorithm must search for the correct root in a subgroup of size 2^S.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

To compute the transitive closure of a directed graph on n vertices using the Floyd-Warshall-style approach with bitset optimization, what is the time complexity and how is it achieved?

A) O(n^3 / w) where w is the machine word size, achieved by storing each row as a bitset and using word-level bitwise OR operations instead of Boolean loops.
B) O(n^2 / w) achieved by using the adjacency matrix in compressed sparse row format.
C) O(n^3 / log n) achieved by Strassen's matrix multiplication on the Boolean semiring.
D) O(n^3) because bitset operations cannot replace the triple-nested loop structure of Floyd-Warshall.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the Stoer-Wagner global minimum cut algorithm, each phase finds a minimum s-t cut between the last two vertices added to the active set. Which property guarantees that taking the minimum over all phases yields the global minimum cut?

A) The algorithm contracts the two vertices connected by the minimum-weight edge at each step, preserving all cut sizes.
B) If the global minimum cut separates the last two vertices merged in a phase, then the phase's cut is the global minimum; otherwise, the two merged vertices can be safely contracted without destroying the global minimum cut.
C) The weight of the cut found in each phase increases monotonically, so the first phase always finds the global minimum.
D) The algorithm explores all possible partitions of the vertex set, so it is guaranteed to find the global minimum by exhaustive search.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the CDQ divide-and-conquer algorithm for counting 3D partial orderings (dominance counting of (x, y, z) triples), after sorting by the first dimension x, the algorithm recursively processes left and right halves. Which data structure is used during the merge step to count points from the right half that are dominated by points from the left half?

A) A segment tree keyed by the y-coordinate, with each node storing a balanced BST over z-coordinates.
B) A binary indexed tree (Fenwick tree) over the z-coordinate, where points from the left half are added as they are iterated in y-order, and points from the right half query the BIT to count left points with smaller z.
C) A hash table mapping y-coordinates to the count of points with that y and smaller z.
D) A skip list sorted by z, allowing range queries of how many left points have z below a threshold.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the Knuth optimization for DP: dp[i][j] = min_{k in [i, j-1]} (dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + cost(i, j)). Which condition on the cost function guarantees that the optimal splitting point opt[i][j] is monotonic (opt[i][j-1] <= opt[i][j] <= opt[i+1][j])?

A) cost(i, j) satisfies the quadrangle inequality and is monotone in the interval containment order.
B) cost(i, j) is convex and differentiable.
C) cost(i, j) depends only on the length j - i, not on the specific endpoints.
D) cost(i, j) is a metric satisfying the triangle inequality.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the Aho-Corasick automaton for multi-pattern matching, what is the purpose of the dictionary suffix link (also called the output link), and how does it differ from the failure link?

A) The dictionary suffix link points from a node to the longest proper suffix that is a terminal node (represents a complete pattern), enabling O(m + z) reporting where z is the total number of matches, while the failure link connects to the longest proper suffix that is a prefix of any pattern.
B) The dictionary suffix link is the same as the failure link, used for transitions when a character does not match.
C) The dictionary suffix link points to the parent node in the trie, while the failure link points to the sibling node.
D) The dictionary suffix link is used during the build phase only, while the failure link is used during the search phase.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Which of the following correctly distinguishes Monte Carlo algorithms from Las Vegas algorithms for decision problems?

A) Monte Carlo algorithms run in worst-case polynomial time but may err with bounded probability; Las Vegas algorithms always produce the correct answer but have expected polynomial running time with unbounded worst-case.
B) Monte Carlo algorithms use randomness only for pivot selection, while Las Vegas algorithms use randomness for all internal decisions.
C) Monte Carlo algorithms are derandomizable via the method of conditional expectations, while Las Vegas algorithms are not.
D) Las Vegas algorithms are a subclass of Monte Carlo algorithms where the error probability is zero.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the simplex method for linear programming, Bland's rule (smallest-index rule) is used for pivot selection. Which of the following statements about Bland's rule is correct?

A) Bland's rule guarantees termination in a polynomial number of pivots, matching the ellipsoid method's complexity.
B) Bland's rule prevents cycling by selecting the smallest-index entering variable among those with positive reduced cost, and the smallest-index leaving variable among eligible candidates, but the worst-case number of pivots remains exponential.
C) Bland's rule prevents cycling only for non-degenerate problems; degeneracy still permits cycling.
D) Bland's rule guarantees that the algorithm terminates in at most m + n pivots, where m is the number of constraints and n is the number of variables.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the context of the suffix array and LCP array, consider the Cartesian tree built from the LCP array. Which of the following correctly relates properties of this Cartesian tree to the structure of the suffix tree?

A) The Cartesian tree of the LCP array is isomorphic to the suffix tree with all suffix nodes removed, where each internal node corresponds to an LCP value representing the longest common prefix of its child suffixes.
B) The Cartesian tree of the LCP array is equivalent to the suffix automaton's state transition graph.
C) The Cartesian tree of the LCP array has leaf nodes corresponding to the Burrows-Wheeler transform characters.
D) The Cartesian tree of the suffix array indices represents the suffix tree's suffix links.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider Konig's theorem relating maximum bipartite matching to minimum vertex cover. Given a bipartite graph G = (L, R, E) and a maximum matching M, which of the following correctly describes how to construct a minimum vertex cover?

A) Include all vertices that participate in M, regardless of which side they belong to.
B) From all free vertices in L, run an alternating BFS in the residual graph. The minimum vertex cover is (L \ Z) union (R intersect Z), where Z is the set of vertices reachable from the free L vertices via alternating paths.
C) Take all vertices in L that are matched and all vertices in R that are unmatched.
D) The minimum vertex cover is exactly the set of vertices incident to the edges of a maximum matching.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

For the Christofides algorithm for the metric TSP to yield a Hamiltonian cycle whose total length is at most 1.5 times the optimal, which of the following conditions must the distance metric satisfy?

A) The distances must be symmetric and satisfy the triangle inequality d(i, k) <= d(i, j) + d(j, k) for all triples.
B) The distances must be Euclidean (L2 norm in R^d), because the algorithm relies on geometric properties.
C) The distances must satisfy the reverse triangle inequality d(i, j) >= |d(i, k) - d(k, j)|.
D) The distances must be integer-valued and all distinct to guarantee the 1.5 factor.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the Miller-Rabin primality test. For the composite number n = 2047 = 23 * 89, what is the result when tested with base a = 2, and why?

A) The test correctly reports composite because 2 is a witness for all odd composites less than 2048.
B) The test incorrectly reports prime because 2047 is a strong pseudoprime to base 2: in the decomposition 2046 = 1023 * 2^1, we have 2^1023 mod 2047 = 1, so the test fails to detect compositeness.
C) The test correctly reports prime because 2047 is actually prime, and the factorization is erroneous.
D) The test incorrectly reports prime because 2047 is a Carmichael number, making any base fail as a witness.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Lagrange polynomial interpolation with n points (x_i, y_i) where the x_i form an arithmetic progression x_i = x_0 + i*h, which technique allows evaluating the interpolating polynomial at a new point x in O(n) time instead of the standard O(n^2)?

A) Using the barycentric form: L(x) = sum_i y_i * (w_i / (x - x_i)) / sum_i (w_i / (x - x_i)), where the weights w_i = 1 / prod_{j != i} (x_i - x_j) can be precomputed in O(n) using prefix and suffix products since the denominators form a binomial pattern.
B) Using Neville's algorithm and caching intermediate results from previous evaluations.
C) Using the Newton divided-difference form with O(n^2) preprocessing that is amortized over many queries.
D) Using FFT-based evaluation where the polynomial is evaluated at all n-th roots of unity simultaneously.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the successive shortest augmenting path algorithm for minimum-cost maximum flow, after the initial Bellman-Ford computation to determine potentials pi(v), why does Dijkstra's algorithm correctly compute shortest paths in subsequent iterations?

A) Because all edge costs in the original graph are non-negative, making Bellman-Ford unnecessary for subsequent computations.
B) Because the reduced cost c_pi(u, v) = c(u, v) + pi(u) - pi(v) is guaranteed to be non-negative for every edge (u, v) that has residual capacity, and the potentials are updated after each augmentation to preserve non-negativity.
C) Because Dijkstra's algorithm works with negative edges as long as the graph is directed and acyclic.
D) Because Bellman-Ford is re-run after every augmentation, so Dijkstra is not actually used.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Edmonds' Blossom algorithm for maximum matching in general (non-bipartite) graphs, an odd-length alternating cycle called a blossom is found during the search for an augmenting path. What is the correct approach for handling blossoms?

A) Blossoms are discarded because they cannot be part of any augmenting path; the DFS backtracks and tries a different route.
B) The blossom is contracted (shrunk) into a single supernode, since any augmenting path entering the blossom can be rerouted through it. The search continues on the contracted graph, and the blossom is expanded when reconstructing the final augmenting path.
C) The blossom indicates that the current matching is already maximum, so the algorithm terminates.
D) All vertices in the blossom are marked as visited and excluded from future DFS searches.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Tarjan's algorithm for finding bridges in an undirected graph, let disc[u] be the discovery time of vertex u during DFS, and low[u] be the lowest discovery time reachable from u or its descendants via a single back edge. Which condition correctly identifies whether a tree edge (u, v) (where u is the parent of v in the DFS tree) is a bridge?

A) low[v] >= disc[u]
B) low[v] > disc[u]
C) low[v] < disc[u]
D) low[u] > disc[v]

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the Hungarian algorithm for the assignment problem, the potentials l(u) for left vertices and r(v) for right vertices satisfy l(u) + r(v) <= cost(u, v) for all u in L, v in R. When the equality graph (edges where l(u) + r(v) == cost(u, v)) does not contain a perfect matching, how are the potentials updated to include at least one new edge while maintaining feasibility?

A) For all u in the alternating tree's left side S, decrease l(u) by delta; for all v in the alternating tree's right side T, increase r(v) by delta, where delta = min_{u in S, v not in T} (cost(u, v) - l(u) - r(v)).
B) Increase all l(u) by delta and decrease all r(v) by delta, where delta = min remaining slack.
C) Multiply all potentials by a factor of 2, then normalize by subtracting the minimum slack.
D) Set l(u) = min_v cost(u, v) for all u and r(v) = 0 for all v, rebuilding the potentials from scratch.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the Z-algorithm for computing the Z-array of a string s, where Z[i] is the length of the longest common prefix of s and s[i:]. The algorithm maintains an interval [l, r] representing the rightmost segment matching the prefix. Which of the following correctly states how Z[i] is initialized when i is within the current interval?

A) Z[i] is initialized to min(Z[i - l], r - i + 1), and then extended by character comparisons.
B) Z[i] is always initialized to 0 and computed from scratch by comparing s[i:] to s[0:].
C) Z[i] is initialized to r - i, using the known matching prefix length from the current interval.
D) Z[i] is initialized to Z[i - l] regardless of the current interval boundaries.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Manacher's algorithm for finding palindromic substrings, the algorithm maintains a center C and a right boundary R representing the palindrome that extends farthest to the right seen so far. What invariant do C and R satisfy?

A) R is the rightmost index reached by any palindrome centered at any position <= C, and C is the center of the palindrome that reaches R.
B) C is always the center of the longest palindrome in the entire string, and R is its right extent.
C) R is the total length of the string, and C cycles through all positions from 0 to n-1.
D) C and R represent the center and radius of the most recently discovered palindrome, regardless of whether it extends farthest.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

For the Hopcroft-Karp algorithm, consider the effect of one complete BFS + DFS phase. Which of the following correctly characterizes the distance from any free left vertex to any free right vertex after one full phase?

A) The distance remains the same if no augmenting path of the current shortest length exists, and the algorithm terminates.
B) The distance between any free left vertex and any free right vertex strictly increases after each phase, because all augmenting paths of the current shortest length become saturated.
C) The distance may decrease if a new augmenting path with fewer edges appears after augmentations.
D) The distance is unchanged, but the matching size increases by at most 2 per phase.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Strassen's matrix multiplication algorithm for n x n matrices where n = 2^k, what is the exact recurrence for the number of scalar additions and subtractions A(n) (not counting the multiplication of submatrices)?

A) A(n) = 7 * A(n/2) + 18 * (n/2)^2
B) A(n) = 7 * A(n/2) + 12 * (n/2)^2
C) A(n) = 7 * A(n/2) + 24 * (n/2)^2
D) A(n) = 8 * A(n/2) + 18 * (n/2)^2

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

For generating a De Bruijn sequence B(k, n) over an alphabet of size k with order n, the FKM (Fredricksen-Kessler-Maiorana) algorithm generates the sequence by concatenating which set of strings in lexicographic order?

A) All k^n possible strings of length n, sorted lexicographically.
B) All Lyndon words whose length divides n, over the given alphabet, sorted lexicographically.
C) All primitive necklaces of length n, sorted in reverse lexicographic order.
D) All aperiodic prefixes of the n-th power of each alphabet symbol.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Pollard's Rho integer factorization algorithm using Floyd's cycle detection, the sequence x_{i+1} = (x_i^2 + c) mod n defines a random walk modulo n. What is the expected number of iterations before a collision modulo a prime factor p is found?

A) O(sqrt(p)) iterations, by the birthday paradox, giving an overall expected O(n^{1/4}) for n = p * q with p approx q.
B) O(log p) iterations, by the properties of quadratic residues.
C) O(p^{2/3}) iterations by the Pollard-Strassen bound.
D) O(sqrt(n)) iterations in the worst case, regardless of the factor size.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the context of the FM-index for exact pattern matching using backward search, what does the LF-mapping (last-to-first mapping) compute?

A) Given a position i in the Burrows-Wheeler transform (last column L), LF(i) returns the position of the same suffix in the first column F of the Burrows-Wheeler matrix, enabling the backward search procedure.
B) LF(i) maps the i-th character of the original text to its position in the sorted suffix array.
C) LF(i) computes the number of occurrences of a character c up to position i in the BWT.
D) LF(i) returns the rank of the suffix starting at position i in the original text.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider using bitset operations (bit parallelism) to compute the longest common subsequence (LCS) of two strings of lengths n and m (n <= m). Using Myers' bit-vector algorithm, what is the time complexity?

A) O(n * m / w) where w is the machine word size, because the DP recurrence can be computed using word-level parallel operations on bit vectors.
B) O(n + m + |Sigma|) because the bit-vector approach eliminates all DP computations.
C) O(n * log m) because each position requires binary search on bit vectors.
D) O(n * m / (w * log |Sigma|)) due to alphabet compression.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the Gomory-Hu tree construction for an undirected graph G = (V, E) with non-negative edge capacities, which of the following properties does the resulting tree T = (V, F) satisfy?

A) For every pair of vertices (u, v), the minimum s-t cut value in G equals the minimum edge weight on the unique path between u and v in T, and T can be constructed using V - 1 maximum flow computations.
B) T contains exactly one edge for each minimum cut in G, and the edge weights are the capacities of these cuts.
C) T is a minimum spanning tree of G with respect to cut capacities as edge weights.
D) T is a tree where each edge represents a pair of vertices that are not separated by any minimum cut.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the context of the convex hull trick (CHT) for DP optimization, when lines are added with decreasing slopes and queries are for increasing x-values, what data structure achieves O(1) amortized time per operation?

A) A balanced binary search tree (e.g., std::set), because the line insertions are arbitrary.
B) A Li Chao segment tree with O(log C) per operation.
C) A deque that maintains the convex hull: lines are added at one end, and queries pop from the other end.
D) A priority queue keyed by the intersection points of adjacent lines.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the push-relabel maximum flow algorithm, what is the purpose of the global relabeling heuristic, and how often is it typically applied?

A) It periodically recomputes exact distances to the sink using reverse BFS from the sink and reassigns vertex heights to these exact distances, typically after Omega(E) relabel operations.
B) It randomly permutes the vertex ordering to break worst-case adversary patterns, applied before each push phase.
C) It merges all vertices with height greater than V into a single super-sink, applied once at the start.
D) It computes a new scaling factor for flow augmentation, applied after every V^2 pushes.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the capacity scaling variant of Dinic's maximum flow algorithm. Starting with a threshold Delta = 2^{floor(log U)} (where U is the maximum edge capacity), each scaling phase considers only edges with residual capacity >= Delta. What is the total number of augmentations across all O(log U) scaling phases?

A) O(E) augmentations per phase, giving O(E log U) total.
B) O(V * E) augmentations per phase, giving O(V * E log U) total.
C) O(log U) augmentations per phase, giving O(log^2 U) total.
D) O(E * sqrt(V)) augmentations per phase, matching the standard Dinic bound.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Boruvka's algorithm for computing the minimum spanning tree, each phase performs one parallel step. Which of the following best describes the reduction in the number of components per phase?

A) Each component selects its cheapest outgoing edge, and all selected edges are added simultaneously. Since each edge connects two components, the number of components at least halves, giving at most O(log V) phases.
B) Each component selects its cheapest outgoing edge, and only edges that do not create cycles are added, reducing the component count by exactly 1 per phase.
C) Components are merged in pairs, reducing the count by exactly half each phase.
D) The number of components reduces by exactly sqrt(V) per phase, requiring O(sqrt(V)) total phases.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In Johnson's algorithm for all-pairs shortest paths in a directed graph with arbitrary edge weights (but no negative cycles), a new vertex s is added with zero-weight edges to all original vertices. Bellman-Ford is run from s to compute potentials pi(v). After reweighting each edge (u, v) with reduced cost c'(u, v) = w(u, v) + pi(u) - pi(v), what is the overall time complexity?

A) O(V * E + V^2 log V) = O(V * E + V * (E + V log V)): one Bellman-Ford (O(V*E)) and V Dijkstra calls using Fibonacci heaps.
B) O(V * E * log V): Bellman-Ford followed by V Dijkstra calls with binary heaps.
C) O(V^3): Bellman-Ford followed by Floyd-Warshall for the reweighted graph.
D) O(E + V log V): because the reweighting eliminates all negative edges, making Dijkstra O(1) per query.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the problem of computing the longest increasing subsequence (LIS) of an array of length n. Using patience sorting, the algorithm maintains a list of piles where each pile's top card is the smallest possible tail value for an increasing subsequence of that length. What is the overall time complexity and how are the piles searched?

A) O(n log n) using binary search on the pile tops to find the leftmost pile whose top is >= the current element.
B) O(n sqrt(n)) using the Van Emde Boas tree over the value domain.
C) O(n log log n) using a segment tree over the compressed value domain.
D) O(n^2) because each element requires scanning all existing piles.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In the Dinic maximum flow algorithm, after the BFS phase builds the level graph, the DFS phase sends blocking flow. What is the worst-case time complexity of one DFS blocking flow computation if implemented with the standard pointer technique (current arc / edge iterator)?

A) O(E) per DFS path, giving O(V * E) worst-case for a full blocking flow.
B) O(E * V) because each DFS path may backtrack O(V) times.
C) O(E) total for the entire blocking flow because each edge is processed at most once across all DFS calls due to the current arc pointer.
D) O(V^2) because each vertex is visited at most once per level.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In a Fibonacci heap, what is the amortized time complexity of the decrease-key operation, and what data structure invariant makes this possible?

A) O(1) amortized, achieved by cutting the node from its parent and adding it to the root list without rebalancing the entire heap, combined with cascading cuts that preserve the heap's potential function bound.
B) O(log n) amortized, because the decrease-key may trigger a cascading series of cuts that propagate up the tree.
C) O(1) worst-case, achieved by always marking nodes after one child loss and cutting after a second loss.
D) O(log n) worst-case, because the heap structure must be restored by sifting up, similar to a binary heap.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

Consider the van Emde Boas layout for storing a complete binary tree in memory to achieve cache-obliviousness. The tree of height h is recursively split into a top tree of height h/2 and bottom subtrees of height h/2. What is the cache complexity of a root-to-leaf traversal with this layout, assuming a cache with block size B?

A) O(log n) memory transfers.
B) O(log_B n) memory transfers.
C) O(log log n) memory transfers.
D) O(log (n/B)) memory transfers.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In a red-black tree with the standard five properties (every node is red or black; root is black; leaves are black; red nodes have black children; all paths from root to leaves have the same number of black nodes), after a standard BST deletion followed by the deletion fixup procedure, what does the concept of a double-black node represent?

A) A node that is colored both red and black simultaneously, maintaining an extra unit of blackness to compensate for a deleted black node.
B) A node that has two black children, both of which are leaves.
C) A node that has been visited twice during the fixup procedure and requires special handling.
D) A node whose black height is greater than 1, indicating that the tree is unbalanced.

Answer with a single letter A, B, C, or D.

In a persistent segment tree implemented via path copying, given an initial array of size n and a sequence of m point updates (each creating a new version), what is the total number of nodes allocated across all versions?

A) O(n + m log n) nodes, because each update creates O(log n) new nodes along the path from root to leaf, while the remaining nodes are shared with the previous version.
